scenario.description: A community gardener with one unused raised bed must decide whether to let an interested gardener use it under an informal produce-and-labor exchange, then settle the growing plan and terms after the regular garden check-in.

shared_context.S1: Mara has one unused 4-by-8-foot raised bed at the neighborhood community garden.
shared_context.S2: The bed is available for one growing arrangement from July 1 through October 31.
shared_context.S3: Mara decides who will use the bed and the final terms of the arrangement.
shared_context.S4: The garden's regular Saturday check-in uses recorded updates: each interested gardener states exact offer terms, Keiko records any site measurement, and Mara decides after all scheduled updates are given.
shared_context.S5: Mara has told the group that, when offers are otherwise workable, she prefers an arrangement that combines cash with useful garden labor and returned produce rather than a cash-only offer.
shared_context.S6: Under the check-in routine, Keiko must enter each site measurement as a formal reveal with the measurement's fact recorded before discussing planting, rather than merely mentioning it in conversation; once an offer is entered as the exact offer for comparison, its amount is not revised during that check-in.

PF1.text: Jonah's proposal is to use the bed from July 1 through October 31, pay Mara $40, contribute six hours of compost work, return four baskets of produce, and water the bed every Tuesday and Friday.

PF2.text: Keiko's recent light measurement shows that this bed receives exactly five hours of direct sun per day; leafy greens are suitable there, but tomatoes are not.

PF3.text: Luis's exact offer for comparison is $60 in cash for the same July 1 through October 31 use, with no compost-work contribution; he will keep this offer unchanged during the check-in.

acceptance_conditions: The bed must be assigned to Jonah.
The use period must run from July 1 through October 31.
The exchange must include exactly $40, six hours of compost work, and four baskets of returned produce, with watering every Tuesday and Friday.
The crop plan must include leafy greens.
Jonah must commit to watering on Tuesday and Friday.
The settlement must record Luis's exactly $60 cash alternative.
Keiko's sunlight measurement must be cited in the justification for the crop plan.

content_checks.C2: decisions['cash_payment'] == 40 and decisions['compost_work_hours'] == 6 and decisions['produce_return_baskets'] == 4 and 'Tuesday' in decisions['watering_days'] and 'Friday' in decisions['watering_days']
content_checks.C4: 'leafy greens' in decisions['crop_plan'] or 'Leafy greens' in decisions['crop_plan']

decisive_facts.why: Jonah's exact proposal changes the settlement to Jonah, fixes the July 1-to-October 31 period, sets $40 plus six compost-work hours and four produce baskets, and specifies Tuesday-and-Friday watering.
The exact five-hour sunlight measurement changes the crop plan from an unspecified planting choice to a leafy-greens plan and requires Keiko's formally revealed site finding to be cited.
Luis's exact unchanged cash offer changes the comparison record to the specific $60 alternative rather than an unspecified or revised cash benchmark.
